title: The one great battle of the revolt. The Toledan host, 4,900 strong, comes against the Emperor's 10,600 at Munt Šāqir in the hills of Extremadura, and is broken

data.note: losses are those on Trent's screen while the battle was under way on 22 February; the outcome is from Trent's account

source: Trent's account and battle screen, 22 February 1383

title: At Jayyān the Emperor runs down the last Toledan army: all 1,807 are lost, for 44 of ours. The revolt ends the same day
source: Trent's account and battle screen, 30 April 1383

title: The so-called Kingdom of Toledo is no more. With its last army destroyed at Jayyān, the revolt ends, five months after it began, and its towns return to the Emperor

data.note: the return of all 58 towns is expected from the revolt's end; a save will confirm it

title: With the realm finally secure, the Emperor takes up the pilgrimage he put off in 774 until the truces had run out and the wars were fought. The next Hajj falls in Dhū al-Ḥijja 785, at the start of February 1384

nextHajj.hijri: 8–13 Dhū al-Ḥijja 785 (tabular calendar; may be a day or two off)

data.truces: Castile, Portugal and Rome to 6 April 1393; Sicily to 15 April 1386; no truce ends near the pilgrimage
